title: Veiled Pathways: Investigating Covert and Side Channels Within GPU Uncore
problem: GPU uncore components (DRAM, NVENC, NVDEC, NVJPEG, host-GPU links, inter-GPU links) remain largely unexplored for side and covert channel vulnerabilities. These non-computational GPU engines can leak sensitive information through frequency scaling, accelerator utilization, and bandwidth allocation side channels.
motivation: As GPUs become primary compute engines in security-critical systems, comprehensive security analysis of all GPU components including uncore is essential for protecting sensitive data.
method: The researchers found four information leaks in GPU support hardware: changes in memory speed (DRAM frequency scaling), and activity levels of the video encoder (NVENC), video decoder (NVDEC), and JPEG processor (NVJPEG). When multiple programs share a GPU through MPS mode, an attacker can observe these leaks by monitoring the data flowing between the CPU and GPU (over PCI-e connections) or between multiple GPUs (over inter-GPU links). They demonstrated attacks using these observations to bypass NVIDIA's GPU MIG isolation system (which normally keeps different programs' work separate) without needing administrator access.
key_novelty: The first systematic way to exploit information leaks (side channels) in GPU support components—DRAM, NVENC, NVDEC, NVJPEG—to circumvent NVIDIA's GPU MIG isolation without requiring administrator access.
contributions: Discovery of four novel leakage sources in GPU uncore including DRAM frequency scaling and hardware accelerator utilization channels
Practical covert and side channel attacks demonstrable under GPU MPS virtualization mode on both desktop and server GPUs
Reevaluation of PCI-e bandwidth allocation and inter-GPU link leakage vectors
Proof-of-concept exploits bypassing NVIDIA GPU MIG hardware isolation on server-scale GPUs

metrics.other: Side channel information leakage capacity and attack feasibility
